items.text: Munoz completed a permanent GBP22m move from Crystal Palace to Nottingham Forest, a three-year deal and a direct request from Oliver Glasner, who managed him before. He was a regular starter and a key contributor at Palace, so his 0.36 availability on your board is the same new-club discount hitting Marmoush, not a form or fitness concern - treat him as a starter, not a bench risk.

Reversing the bench read published last night: multiple reports now have Garner set to start for Everton against Manchester United on Sunday, with Hackney a doubt after picking up a knock. Sky Sports says Garner is playing well enough to be linked with an England call-up.

Leeds boss Daniel Farke confirmed centre-back rival Joe Rodon has a hamstring injury and will be out for eight to ten weeks, removing Bijol's main competition for a starting spot for the rest of this international window and beyond.

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said Marmoush is available to play, possibly from kickoff, against Forest - direct manager confirmation for a player who only just arrived on loan from Man City alongside Savio. The model's availability figure has been rising with the news but is still a step behind what the manager is actually saying.

runs.note: seeded by hand while building the pipeline
Garner's pre-season groin surgery - explains an availability number the model could only read as 'not playing'

Marmoush (Man City to Spurs, started and impressed on debut) and Munoz (Palace to Forest, permanent, Glasner's man) both hit the same new-club-discount blind spot the model has for Barcola - both are mine, both look like bench risks on the dashboard and are actually starters
Woltemade (mine, weakest forward) loaned out to Juventus on deadline day - he is out of the Premier League entirely, not just out of favour, which the 0.37 availability figure did not capture

Munoz correction (he's competing with Aina for the RB spot, not a guaranteed starter as reported yesterday), Garner benefiting from Hackney's ankle knock, and Palace's Mateta hamstring injury opening the door for free agents Strand Larsen and Nketiah

Leeds' Rodon (hamstring) and Gruev (meniscus) both sidelined, thinning the competition for Bijol's centre-back spot. Checked rivals' best assets (Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo, Guehi, Dewsbury-Hall) for league-scope news but every lead traced back to stale Dec 2025/pre-season stories, not current - nothing else published this run

Ran club-by-club searches on every squad member and free-agent target (Munoz/Aina, Garner, Bijol's rivals, Woltemade, Palace strikers, Bournemouth and Brighton free agents) but every lead just re-confirmed what was already published earlier today - the one new item was a fresh (17:10 UTC) pundit piece projecting Marmoush inside Tottenham's actual strongest XI going forward, not just a one-off debut start, which the model's 0.35 availability still does not reflect

Munoz reversal - Forest's own predicted XI (published this morning) has him starting at right wing-back against Spurs, not competing with Aina as reported Tuesday, so he comes off the drop list this week; and Barcola is now confirmed live in the FPL pool with a possible bench debut Friday at Ipswich, still rated near the bottom of all free agents by the model. Full club-by-club refresh (Everton, Arsenal, Forest, City, Leeds, Brentford, Fulham, Bournemouth, Tottenham, Newcastle, Brighton) plus rivals' best assets (Bruno Fernandes, Palmer, Gibbs-White, Semenyo) found nothing else new or actionable

Full deep-research pass ahead of GW3's deadline (squad now final after waivers processed): corrected Tuesday's misread on Garner (he was a sub, not a starter, at Preston - he's behind Hackney for Sunday), found Doku's calf return has slipped to 13 September (GW4) not the 5 September date shown on the dashboard, and confirmed Igor Jesus as Forest's nailed-on striker ahead of Chris Wood in red-hot preseason form. Also ran a full club-by-club sweep across all 15 squad players for starters.json - see claims.json and starters.json for what changed there.

Re-run 13 minutes after the last deep pass ahead of GW3's deadline (17:30 UTC tomorrow). Ran a fresh sweep across every squad club (Everton, Forest, Man City, Leeds, Bournemouth, Brentford, Palace, Tottenham, Liverpool, Sunderland) plus rivals' best assets - Rodon's 8-10 week hamstring, Doku's calf, Munoz's Forest debut, Marmoush vs Solanke, and Barcola's expected bench debut are all confirmed exactly as already published this evening. One search flagged a possible Solanke ankle knock, but a follow-up read found only stale July/August articles referencing his prior surgery, not a current one, so nothing new to add or correct.

Full club-by-club sweep ~11 hours ahead of the GW3 deadline (17:30 UTC). Two corrections against last night's read: Garner is now set to start against Man Utd (Hackney a doubt with a knock), and Solanke's ankle injury (out since early August, major doubt) removes the competition threat to Marmoush that was cited last night, with Marmoush now in Tottenham's predicted XI. Also checked Brentford (two search hits on Schade/Collins injuries turned out to be stale articles from a prior season and were discarded), Leeds (Bijol still locked in alongside new signing Elvedi), Bournemouth (Hill, Rayan, Tavernier all in the predicted XI), Crystal Palace (Strand Larsen confirmed starting with Mateta out until October) and Liverpool (Barcola still expected on the bench for his debut at Ipswich tonight) - all unchanged from what's already published.
dropped 17 of 19 items whose only citation was off the SOURCES list

Two items the source purge had removed, republished with permitted citations found this run: Rodon's 8-10 week hamstring injury (clears Bijol's path at Leeds, leedsunited.com) and De Zerbi confirming Marmoush available, possibly from the start, against Forest (tottenhamhotspur.com). Also re-sourced starters.json and claims.json this run - see their own run logs. Nothing else material found in a fresh club-by-club sweep, including a check on Strand Larsen (his old 'leading the line' claim did not survive a fresh look at the source, which turned out to be nine months stale, so not republished).

Full club-by-club sweep ~8 hours after the last run (Everton, Arsenal, Forest, Man City, Leeds, Brentford, Liverpool, Bournemouth, Tottenham, Palace, Sunderland) plus two general searches on deadline-day fallout and rivals. Everything already published held up: Garner still favoured in Everton's predicted double pivot for Sunday even with Hackney now cleared of his ankle knock, Bijol has no fresh fitness concern ahead of Brighton, Strand Larsen is confirmed leading the Palace line at Fulham, and Doku's calf timeline still points past GW4's deadline. One lead - conflicting reports that Ola Aina, not Munoz, starts at right wing-back for Forest against Tottenham - never cleared a permitted outlet (only Sports Mole, GiveMeSport and thehardtackle carried it), so it was left out rather than reversing Wednesday's Forest-sourced correction on a weak citation. Nothing else was material enough to publish.
